title: Radioactive decay

data.source: Rutherford, Geiger and Bateman (1910), Phil. Mag. 20, 698-707, table of alpha counts in 2608 intervals of 7.5 s (typed into the script). The seed test uses simulated exponential waits.

prediction: If decays were cuts at a counted threshold, counts in equal windows would be regular: variance/mean below 0.5, and a seed carried from past waits would predict the next wait at least 2 % better than the mean.
baseline: Memoryless decay: Poisson counts with variance/mean = 1, and nothing predicts the next wait better than the long-run mean.
why: Counts are as scattered as chance allows (Fano close to 1, Poisson fits), not regular as a count-to-threshold would make them, and a carried-over seed does not predict the next wait better than the plain mean.
